details:
Project ZERO MERIDIAN – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Project ZERO MERIDIAN is an interactive, space-themed web application designed to introduce children aged 8–14 to space science and astronaut training through engaging, game-based learning. The application provides five interactive missions: Launch Sequence, Orbit Mechanics, Spacewalk Training, Mars Rover Navigation, and Mission Control Quiz.

Each mission introduces important concepts of space exploration. Children can practise launch procedures, understand orbital mechanics, experience simulated zero-gravity activities, navigate planetary surfaces, and test their knowledge through interactive quizzes. The application also integrates NASA's open APIs, including Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD), Mars Rover Photos, Near Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs), and ISS position data, helping learners connect educational activities with real space information.

The platform includes a Mission Hub with a ranking system, experience points (XP), achievement badges, and progress tracking to motivate children. It also provides downloadable astronaut certificates, multilingual support for English, Hindi, and Kannada, accessibility options, and offline access to core missions.

The project was developed using React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Zustand. LocalStorage is used to save player progress without requiring a backend database.

Our creative approach combines interactive simulations, gamification, real NASA resources, and child-friendly design to make complex scientific concepts easier to understand. We considered the target age group, ease of navigation, educational value, accessibility, and mobile responsiveness throughout development.

The intended impact is to make STEM education more engaging and accessible, encourage curiosity about space exploration, and inspire children to develop an interest in science, technology, engineering, and future space missions.
